algorithm.title: Calculation of attributable risk and relative risk in cohort studies

nodes.text: Recognize epidemiological risk measures in prospective cohort studies
Calculate incidence rate in exposed group (Ie): 30 / 1000 = 0.030 (3.0%)
Calculate incidence rate in unexposed group (Iu): 3 / 1000 = 0.003 (0.3%)
Calculate Attributable Risk (AR = Risk Difference): AR = Ie - Iu = 0.030 - 0.003 = 0.027 (2.7%)

**Relative risk (RR):** RR = Ie / Iu = 0.030 / 0.003 = 10.0
Interpret attributable risk as excess disease incidence directly attributable to the exposure

algorithm.title: Intrinsic properties of diagnostic tests: sensitivity and specificity

abdominal-trauma.name: Abdominal trauma
abdominal-trauma.scope: Blunt abdominal trauma (splenic/hepatic laceration, FAST exam, CT scan), penetrating abdominal trauma (stab, gunshot, peritonitis, exploratory laparotomy indications)
abdominal-trauma.core: Abdominal injury after collision, fall, stabbing, or gunshot: hemodynamic status and peritoneal signs determine imaging versus immediate operation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: High-speed deceleration, seat-belt compression, lower rib fractures; anticoagulation increases bleeding risk
Stab wounds may spare viscera; bullets frequently injure multiple structures

rows.label: Clues
items: LUQ pain or referred left shoulder pain → splenic injury; RUQ tenderness → hepatic injury
Distention, ecchymoses, abdominal wall marks; initially benign examination does not exclude bowel injury
★ **Rigidity, rebound, persistent hypotension**, or evisceration → urgent operative assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Solid-organ disruption → intraperitoneal hemorrhage; mesenteric injury → ischemia or delayed perforation
Retroperitoneal injury may produce little intraperitoneal free fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **FAST** at bedside during resuscitation; detects free fluid, not organ-specific injury
★ Stable → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**; evaluate solid organs, bowel, retroperitoneum
Negative FAST with ongoing shock → search thorax/pelvis, repeat assessment; do not assume safety
Stable anterior stab → local wound exploration or serial examination/CT; trajectory guides evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway, large-bore IV access, warmed blood products; massive transfusion for hemorrhagic shock
★ Unstable + positive FAST, peritonitis, or ongoing transfusion need → **exploratory laparotomy**; no CT delay
Stable splenic/hepatic injury → monitored nonoperative care; blush, transient response → angioembolization (older questions: laparotomy)
Enteric contents, uncontrolled bleeding → operation; transperitoneal gunshot → **laparotomy** even if stable; selected stabs observed
Suspected bowel perforation → ceftriaxone + metronidazole, trauma surgery; free subdiaphragmatic air → **laparotomy**, no CT

rows.label: Complications
items: Delayed splenic rupture, abscess, bile leak, abdominal compartment syndrome

rows.label: Prevention

rows.label: Mimics

abnormal-uterine-bleeding.name: Abnormal uterine bleeding
abnormal-uterine-bleeding.scope: Adenomyosis, leiomyomas, endometrial polyps, ovulatory dysfunction, PALM-COEIN classification, endometrial biopsy

acetaminophen-toxicity.name: Acetaminophen toxicity
acetaminophen-toxicity.scope: Rumack-Matthew nomogram, 4-hour post-ingestion level, toxic metabolite NAPQI, N-acetylcysteine indications and timing, acute liver failure

rows.label: Risk factors

items: ★ Known acute ingestion → **acetaminophen concentration at ≥4 hours**; earlier result cannot risk-stratify
★ Plot **Rumack–Matthew nomogram**, 4–24 h; treatment line starts 150 µg/mL at 4 h

Assess co-ingestions/pregnancy; intentional ingestion → psychiatric safety evaluation after stabilization

rows.label: Mimics

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, cirrhosis, low-output heart failure (prerenal despite overload); baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment (dipstick blood, few RBCs), prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → tubulointerstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**
Anuria despite patent catheter after pelvic surgery + hydronephrosis → ureteral injury/ligation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia (postoperative oliguria, high urine specific gravity) → saline bolus; congestion → loop diuretic; no reflex fluids in overload
Stop nephrotoxins, all NSAIDs including celecoxib (intra-articular steroid for joint pain); persistent AIN → glucocorticoids; renal-dose drugs
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function
Contrast in high-risk CKD → **periprocedural IV isotonic saline**; diuretics, mannitol, metformin stop don't protect
ACR now limits contrast prophylaxis mainly to eGFR <30; older exam questions may expect wider hydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

COPD, neuromuscular weakness, obesity hypoventilation, sedatives → ventilation failure; overlap common

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachypnea, accessory-muscle use, hypoxemia, diaphoresis; hypercapnia may cause headache, somnolence, asterixis
★ **Exhaustion, declining consciousness, silent chest, paradoxical breathing** → impending respiratory arrest
Normal saturation on supplemental oxygen does not exclude dangerous CO₂ retention

rows.label: Pathophys
items: V/Q mismatch, shunt, or diffusion impairment lowers PaO₂; shunt may resist oxygen alone
Inadequate alveolar ventilation raises PaCO₂; abrupt rise causes respiratory acidosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pulse oximetry + ABG** when severe distress, hypercapnia concern, or escalating support
Chest radiograph, ECG, bedside lung/cardiac ultrasound; infection/PE testing follows clinical context
Trend pH, gases, respiratory rate, mentation and effort; do not wait for an extreme number
Chronic compensated hypercapnia has elevated bicarbonate; pH decline identifies acute deterioration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Oxygen immediately**, treat cause; target SpO₂ 88–92% with CO₂-retention risk, usually 92–96% otherwise
Hypoxemic failure needing more than conventional oxygen → high-flow nasal cannula, close reassessment
★ Awake cooperative COPD + respiratory acidosis → **BiPAP**; cardiogenic edema → CPAP/BiPAP plus diuresis/nitrates
★ **Intubate** for airway failure, refractory hypoxemia, shock, arrest, exhaustion, or worsening despite noninvasive support
Avoid NIV with vomiting, unprotected airway, copious secretions, major facial trauma; reassess within 1–2 h

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoxic brain injury, arrhythmia, multiorgan failure; delayed intubation worsens outcome
Positive pressure → hypotension/barotrauma; invasive ventilation → pneumonia and ventilator-induced lung injury
Ventilated ARDS: low tidal volume using predicted body weight, limited plateau pressure; prone if severe

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, respiratory vaccination, disease control, cautious sedatives, aspiration precautions
High-risk extubation patients may benefit from planned NIV rather than rescue after deterioration
Awake, stable, low ventilator support → **spontaneous breathing trial** to wean, before tracheostomy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Metabolic acidosis: compensatory tachypnea with low CO₂
Panic hyperventilation: respiratory alkalosis without sustained gas-exchange failure

table.title: Gas-exchange classification; room air when feasible

acute-rhinosinusitis.name: Acute rhinosinusitis
acute-rhinosinusitis.scope: Common cold, viral rhinosinusitis, acute bacterial rhinosinusitis criteria, symptomatic therapy, antibiotic stewardship
acute-rhinosinusitis.core: Acute nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, and facial pressure usually reflect a self-limited viral infection; duration and course identify likely bacterial disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Respiratory exposure, daycare contacts, impaired drainage from allergic inflammation
Immunocompromise, recent antibiotics, or hospitalization increases resistant-organism risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Cough, reduced smell, maxillary tenderness; colored mucus alone does not establish bacterial infection
★ Orbital swelling, painful eye movement, reduced vision, severe headache → **complicated infection**
Well febrile child, URI symptoms, clear lungs, good perfusion: soft flow murmur innocent, not VSD

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral mucosal edema blocks sinus drainage; secondary infection commonly pneumococcus, H influenzae, or Moraxella

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; uncomplicated illness needs neither sinus radiographs nor CT
Persistent, severe, or biphasic course identifies bacterial cases; fever alone is insufficient
Suspected orbital/intracranial extension → contrast CT; MRI for intracranial definition
Refractory or unusual infection → ENT evaluation; routine nasal swab cultures unhelpful

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Viral illness → **saline irrigation, acetaminophen/NSAID**, oral pseudoephedrine (not young children); no antibiotics
Intranasal fluticasone for associated allergic inflammation; topical oxymetazoline at most 3 days
★ Uncomplicated bacterial illness + reliable follow-up → **watchful waiting** or antibiotics
Antibiotic choice: amoxicillin-clavulanate, usually 5–7 days in adults; penicillin allergy → doxycycline
Complication → admission, IV ampicillin-sulbactam, urgent ENT/ophthalmology; avoid empiric azithromycin because resistance

rows.label: Complications
items: Orbital cellulitis or abscess, cavernous sinus thrombosis, meningitis, intracranial abscess
Unnecessary antibiotics → diarrhea, C difficile, resistance

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, smoking avoidance, control allergic rhinitis
Sterile/distilled or previously boiled water for nasal irrigation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Allergic rhinitis: itching, sneezing, watery discharge without fever
Migraine: episodic disabling headache, photophobia, nausea
Dental infection: focal tooth pain, unilateral maxillary symptoms

table.title: Bacterial patterns
rows: Initial improvement → new fever or worsening symptoms

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all 19–59; ≥60 with risk/request; health worker anti-HBs negative post-series → revaccinate
**HIV any CD4**, liver disease/alcohol, COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal <50; liver → HepA/HepB
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Anti-HBs/anti-HAV/VZV IgG positive → immune, skip; otherwise **do not delay vaccination** for serology
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **No live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza**: severe immunosuppression, pregnancy (nonimmune → postpartum)
PCV15 → PPSV23: ≥8 weeks immunocompromised; older exams: PPSV23 alone; mild illness/antibiotics: no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern; inactivated influenza cannot cause flu, coincidental virus; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

alcohol-associated-liver-disease.name: Alcohol-associated liver disease
alcohol-associated-liver-disease.scope: Hepatic steatosis, alcoholic hepatitis, alcoholic cirrhosis, AST to ALT ratio greater than 2, GGT elevation, Maddrey discriminant function, prednisolone therapy
alcohol-associated-liver-disease.core: Heavy alcohol use with new jaundice, tender hepatomegaly and modest AST-predominant aminotransferase elevation suggests alcohol-associated hepatitis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sustained heavy alcohol intake; obesity and chronic viral hepatitis accelerate progression

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever in suspected alcohol-associated hepatitis can mimic infection; evaluate before glucocorticoids

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased NADH favors steatosis; acetaldehyde and oxidative injury promote inflammation and fibrosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AST:ALT >2** supportive; both typically <400 in hepatitis; GGT elevation nonspecific
New jaundice with bilirubin >3 mg/dL; exclude infection, viral hepatitis and biliary obstruction
★ Severe hepatitis: **MELD >20** guides steroids; classic **Maddrey DF ≥32**
Maddrey DF = 4.6 × PT prolongation in seconds + bilirubin in mg/dL

rows.label: Tx
items: Abstinence, nutritional support, thiamine; treat withdrawal and alcohol use disorder
★ Severe hepatitis → prednisolone if eligible; defer during uncontrolled infection, GI bleeding or severe renal failure
★ Stop steroids for **Lille >0.45** on day 4 or 7
Decompensated cirrhosis or selected severe refractory hepatitis → transplant evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Portal hypertension, encephalopathy, hepatorenal syndrome, hepatocellular carcinoma; steroids increase infection risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Cirrhosis: HCC surveillance with ultrasound and AFP every 6 months; portal hypertension assessment
HAV and HBV vaccination if nonimmune

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic hepatitis: shock and aminotransferases often in thousands
Biliary obstruction: ductal dilation and predominant alkaline phosphatase elevation

alcohol-associated-liver-disease.evidence: Checked ACG Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease guideline (2024).

alcohol-intoxication.name: Alcohol intoxication
alcohol-intoxication.scope: Acute ethanol intoxication, respiratory depression, metabolic derangements, head trauma co-ingestion, clinical sobriety and discharge criteria
alcohol-intoxication.core: Recent ethanol use with disinhibition, slurred speech, ataxia, and impaired attention; profound obtundation requires evaluation beyond alcohol alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Rapid binge drinking, low tolerance, fasting, extremes of age
Opioids, benzodiazepines, and other sedatives amplify ventilatory suppression

rows.label: Clues
items: Nystagmus, impaired coordination, vomiting, hypothermia; odor neither confirms nor excludes severity
★ Slow or sonorous respirations, absent airway reflexes, hypoxemia → **life-threatening poisoning**
Focal neurologic findings, persistent coma, fever, or deterioration suggest an additional diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Enhanced GABA and inhibited glutamate signaling → dose-dependent CNS depression
Inhibited gluconeogenesis → hypoglycemia, especially with depleted glycogen stores; vomiting promotes electrolyte losses

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside glucose immediately**; serial vitals/neurologic exams; continuous **pulse oximetry, end-tidal CO₂** until awake
Electrolytes, renal function, pregnancy testing when relevant; ethanol level if diagnostic uncertainty
Head CT for trauma, focal deficit, anticoagulation, or unexplained persistent altered mental status
Suspected co-ingestion → acetaminophen/salicylate levels, ECG; osmolar and anion gaps if toxic alcohol possible
Measured alcohol concentration correlates poorly with functional impairment in tolerant drinkers

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway positioning/suction → ventilation or **intubation** if unable to protect airway
★ Low glucose → **IV dextrose immediately**; thiamine before or alongside, never delay glucose
Thiamine for malnutrition or chronic heavy use; suspected Wernicke encephalopathy → parenteral replacement
IV saline for hypovolemia; fluids do not accelerate ethanol clearance; no charcoal for isolated ingestion
Discharge at **clinical sobriety** with capacity, not blood alcohol cutoff; stable vitals, ambulation, oral intake

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration, hypoglycemic injury, trauma, hypothermia, rhabdomyolysis
Withdrawal may emerge during observation as ethanol falls, even before the level reaches zero

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Assess **suicidal intent**, unsafe driving, and alcohol-use disorder after cognition recovers
Brief counseling, treatment linkage, responsible supervision; no driving at discharge

rows.label: Mimics
items: Opioid overdose: pinpoint pupils, naloxone response
Toxic alcohol ingestion: visual injury or renal injury, evolving high anion gap
Stroke: persistent focal deficit rather than global dose-related impairment
Stimulant intoxication: tachycardia, hypertension, dilated pupils; ataxia favors alcohol

alcohol-intoxication.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency toxicology principles.

alcohol-withdrawal.name: Alcohol withdrawal
alcohol-withdrawal.core: Autonomic and neuropsychiatric excitation after reducing prolonged heavy alcohol intake; progression from mild symptoms to life-threatening delirium.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior withdrawal seizures/delirium, repeated detoxifications, heavy sustained use, older age
Acute illness, electrolyte depletion, concurrent sedative dependence; poor support increases outpatient failure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Diaphoresis, tachycardia, hypertension, insomnia, nausea; symptoms possible with **positive blood alcohol**
Hospital day 2–5 or postoperative: new agitation, hallucinations, autonomic signs → suspect **unreported alcohol use**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Chronic ethanol → downregulated GABA inhibition/upregulated NMDA excitation; cessation unmasks neuronal hyperactivity
Repeated episodes → kindling, progressively lower seizure threshold

rows.label: Dx
items: **Clinical diagnosis** + time since reduction; bedside glucose, CBC, electrolytes, Mg, phosphate, liver tests
★ **CIWA-Ar** if communicative; ≥19 severe; delirium/intubation → **RASS/MINDS**
First/focal seizure, head injury, focal deficit, atypical timing → head CT; do not assume withdrawal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Diazepam/chlordiazepoxide** symptom-triggered; liver dysfunction/older frail adults → **lorazepam/oxazepam**
★ Seizures/delirium → monitored inpatient **IV benzodiazepines**; refractory → ICU phenobarbital with respiratory monitoring
★ **Parenteral thiamine**; hypoglycemia → immediate dextrose, never wait; correct electrolyte deficits
Phenytoin ineffective; dexmedetomidine adjunct; **chlorpromazine**/antipsychotics lower seizure threshold, prolong QT

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration, dysrhythmias, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis; excessive sedation → respiratory depression
Malnutrition → Wernicke encephalopathy: confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia; suspected → high-dose IV thiamine
Pregnancy: seizures, adrenergic surge → fetal hypoxia; **maternal withdrawal** is greatest immediate fetal risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: High-risk inpatients → preventive benzodiazepines; outpatient withdrawal only if mild, reliable supervision
Recovery: **naltrexone** unless opioids/acute hepatitis; **acamprosate** unless severe CKD; addiction follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hepatic encephalopathy: asterixis, decompensated cirrhosis, less autonomic excitation
Sepsis: infectious source, hypotension, persistent inflammatory findings
Sedative withdrawal: benzodiazepine/barbiturate reduction; similar syndrome, different exposure
Anticholinergic delirium: dry skin, urinary retention; diaphoresis favors withdrawal

table.title: Approximate onset after reduction; overlap common
rows: Visual/auditory/tactile hallucinations; clear sensorium; vitals near normal
Disorientation, hallucinations, fever, tremor, marked autonomic instability

allergic-rhinitis.name: Allergic rhinitis
allergic-rhinitis.scope: Seasonal and perennial rhinitis, bluish boggy turbinates, allergic shiners, intranasal glucocorticoids, oral antihistamines, allergen avoidance
allergic-rhinitis.core: Recurrent sneezing, nasal itching, and clear rhinorrhea after allergen exposure, often accompanied by itchy watery eyes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Atopy, asthma, eczema, family history; occupational allergen exposure
Seasonal: tree, grass, weed pollens; perennial: dust mites, pets, indoor molds

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Pale bluish boggy turbinates**, allergic shiners, transverse nasal crease
Congestion, postnasal drip, mouth breathing; symptoms impair sleep, school, or work
Fever, purulent unilateral drainage, epistaxis, or focal pain warrants another explanation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links mast-cell IgE → histamine release; late eosinophilic inflammation sustains obstruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis** from reproducible exposure pattern and examination
Uncertain diagnosis, persistent symptoms, or immunotherapy planning → skin-prick or serum allergen-specific IgE testing
Positive sensitization test requires matching exposure history; total IgE and imaging are not routine
Unilateral obstruction → inspect for foreign body, structural lesion, or mass

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Persistent or congestion-dominant disease → **intranasal fluticasone**; direct spray away from septum
Mild intermittent disease → cetirizine or loratadine; intranasal azelastine offers rapid relief
Incomplete control → intranasal steroid + intranasal antihistamine; saline irrigation as adjunct
★ Refractory, confirmed sensitization → **allergen immunotherapy** with allergy specialist
Avoid sedating first-generation antihistamines in older adults; decongestant sprays >3 days → rebound congestion

rows.label: Complications
items: Sleep disruption, reduced concentration, eustachian tube dysfunction, recurrent sinus symptoms
Intranasal steroid misuse → epistaxis; systemic decongestants → hypertension, tachycardia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Allergen reduction**: mattress encasements, hot-wash bedding, moisture control, exposure-directed pet avoidance
Close windows during high pollen periods; avoid tobacco smoke and personal irritants

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral URI: short course, malaise, possible fever
Nonallergic rhinitis: odor/temperature triggers, little itching, negative sensitization testing
Rhinitis medicamentosa: chronic topical vasoconstrictor use with rebound blockage

allergic-rhinitis.evidence: Not checked online; established rhinitis diagnostic and treatment principles.

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

anaphylaxis.name: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.scope: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, biphasic reactions, epinephrine autoinjector, emergency airway management
anaphylaxis.core: Rapid multisystem reaction after exposure—or isolated hypotension or airway compromise after a known allergen—requires epinephrine immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Foods, insect venom, antibiotics, latex; exercise can amplify food-triggered reactions
Asthma, prior severe reaction, mast-cell disorders; beta-blockers can complicate treatment

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Urticaria/angioedema + wheeze, stridor, hypotension, or severe GI symptoms**
Skin findings may be absent; hoarseness and tongue swelling predict airway danger
Biphasic recurrence after apparent resolution, especially after severe or undertreated episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mast-cell/basophil mediators → vasodilation, capillary leak, bronchoconstriction; often IgE-mediated
Epinephrine: α1 reverses vasodilation/edema, β2 reverses bronchoconstriction; albuterol alone misses edema and shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; never wait for tryptase or laboratory confirmation
Acute and baseline serum tryptase can support uncertain cases; normal results do not exclude anaphylaxis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IM epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg**, adult 0.3–0.5 mg, lateral thigh; repeat every 5–15 minutes
Supine with legs elevated unless respiratory distress; oxygen, early intubation for progressive obstruction
Profound shock or refractory hypotension → titrated IV epinephrine plus **isotonic boluses**; beta-blocker use → glucagon
Albuterol for residual bronchospasm; antihistamines relieve itching only; steroids do not reliably prevent biphasic reactions
★ Monitor until resolved; **longer observation/admission** after hypotension, repeated epinephrine, or severe asthma

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxia, distributive shock, arrhythmia, hypoxic brain injury
Undiluted IV epinephrine bolus errors → ischemia and dangerous dysrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prescribe **epinephrine autoinjector**, demonstrate technique, provide written action plan and allergy referral
Extra device for repeat-dose risk; avoidance, medical alert ID; venom immunotherapy after qualifying sting allergy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal episode: bradycardia, pallor, rapid improvement supine
Bradykinin angioedema: no itching/hives; ACE inhibitor or hereditary disease → airway, icatibant/C1 inhibitor

antepartum-bleeding.name: Antepartum bleeding
antepartum-bleeding.scope: Placenta previa, placental abruption, vasa previa, uterine rupture, transabdominal ultrasound before digital exam, Kleihauer-Betke test, emergent cesarean delivery
antepartum-bleeding.core: Bleeding in later pregnancy requires immediate maternal stabilization and fetal assessment, followed by placental localization before any digital cervical examination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previa: prior cesarean, multiparity; abruption: hypertension, cocaine, trauma, prior abruption
Vasa previa: velamentous cord, accessory placental lobe, IVF; rupture: uterine scar, obstructed labor

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock may exceed visible blood loss** with concealed abruption or internal hemorrhage
Assess uterine tone, pain, contractions, fetal tracing, membrane status; bleeding volume alone is unreliable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal placental bleeding versus fetal vessel hemorrhage; vasa previa can rapidly exsanguinate fetus
Placental separation or uterine disruption compromises oxygen delivery independent of maternal external blood loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC, type/crossmatch, coagulation studies including fibrinogen; continuous fetal monitoring if viable
★ **Ultrasound before digital examination**; transabdominal first; transvaginal safely clarifies placenta–cervix relationship
Normal ultrasound does not exclude abruption; suspected rupture is a clinical emergency
Rh-negative bleeding/trauma → Kleihauer–Betke or flow cytometry quantifies fetomaternal hemorrhage for anti-D dosing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ ABCs, two large IVs, blood products when needed; **do not delay delivery for imaging if unstable**
Hemorrhage/fetal compromise → emergency cesarean; rupture → laparotomy, uterine repair or hysterectomy
Stable preterm previa → observation, pelvic rest, corticosteroids when eligible; planned cesarean before labor
Abruption: deliver if significant or compromised; vaginal birth possible when stable and imminent or fetal demise
Unsensitized Rh-negative patient → anti-D immunoglobulin; correct abruption-associated coagulopathy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, DIC, AKI, hysterectomy; fetal hypoxia, death, prematurity
Previa plus cesarean scar increases placenta accreta spectrum risk and operative hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP, avoid cocaine/tobacco; prenatal placental/cord localization and planned high-risk delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bloody show: small mucus-streaked bleeding with cervical change
Cervical lesion: contact bleeding, visible source on speculum examination

table.title: Critical distinctions
rows: Bleeding after rupture; sudden fetal bradycardia
Scarred uterus; sudden pain, lost station, fetal bradycardia

antepartum-bleeding.evidence: Not checked online; established obstetric hemorrhage teaching.

antidepressants.name: Antidepressants
antidepressants.scope: SSRIs, SNRIs, bupropion, mirtazapine, tricyclic antidepressants (anticholinergic toxicity, urinary retention, arrhythmia), MAO inhibitors, adverse effects (serotonin syndrome)
antidepressants.core: SSRIs usually start depression treatment; choose alternatives by accompanying symptoms, adverse effects, and overdose risk.

rows.label: Use
items: SSRIs/SNRIs: depression, anxiety; duloxetine also neuropathic pain
Bupropion: smoking cessation; mirtazapine: poor appetite with insomnia
TCAs/MAOIs: resistant depression; TCAs also neuropathic pain

rows.label: Mechanism
items: SSRIs: serotonin reuptake blockade; SNRIs/TCAs: serotonin + norepinephrine reuptake blockade
Bupropion: norepinephrine/dopamine reuptake blockade; mirtazapine: α2 antagonism
MAOIs: reduced monoamine degradation

rows.label: Adverse
items: SSRIs: GI upset, SIADH, bleeding; SNRIs: ↑BP; mirtazapine: sedation/weight gain; bupropion: activating
★ SSRI **sexual dysfunction** → **lower dose** first; other SSRIs rarely help; bupropion minimal
TCAs: constipation, urinary retention, conduction toxicity; MAOIs: orthostatic hypotension

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ Bupropion lowers seizure threshold: **seizure or eating disorders**; CYP inhibitors raise levels
TCAs: urinary retention, glaucoma, conduction disease; anticholinergic delirium in older adults
TCA therapy with QTc/QRS prolongation → **stop TCA**, no waiting for levels

rows.label: Interactions
items: MAOI + tyramine/sympathomimetics → hypertensive crisis → **phentolamine** (α-blocker)
MAOI + SSRI/tramadol → serotonin syndrome; washout generally 14 days, after fluoxetine 5 weeks
Fluoxetine/paroxetine inhibit CYP2D6 → ↑TCA levels, toxicity

rows.label: Monitor
items: Mood, suicidality early in young adults; monitor adherence and functioning
Abrupt stop → **discontinuation**: flu-like aches, headache, dizziness, electric paresthesias, nausea, tremor
Response over 4–6 weeks; taper to stop, especially paroxetine and venlafaxine

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Serotonin syndrome**: clonus, fever/agitation → stop drugs, benzodiazepines; cyproheptadine
★ TCA overdose: Na⁺-channel blockade → **wide QRS**, arrhythmia, seizures → IV sodium bicarbonate
Bipolar depression: antidepressant monotherapy may provoke mania

antidepressants.evidence: Not checked online; established pharmacology and prescribing safety.

antipsychotics.name: Antipsychotics
antipsychotics.scope: First-generation vs second-generation, extrapyramidal symptoms (acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia), neuroleptic malignant syndrome, metabolic syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, QTc prolongation
antipsychotics.core: Dopamine-modulating drugs treat psychosis and mania; selection depends on motor, metabolic, endocrine, cardiovascular, and hematologic risks.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Psychosis, mania, agitation; **SGA first-line**; **clozapine** if resistant or recurrent suicidality
FGA: mainly D2 antagonism; SGA: D2/5-HT2 effects, varying by agent
Quetiapine sedation → switch to aripiprazole; obesity → ziprasidone, not olanzapine/clozapine

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Nigrostriatal blockade → movement disorders; tuberoinfundibular blockade → prolactin elevation
Aripiprazole: partial D2 agonist; haloperidol high-potency FGA, chlorpromazine low-potency FGA
Chronic D2 blockade → receptor supersensitivity → tardive dyskinesia; can worsen after stopping

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Fever, **lead-pipe rigidity**, autonomic instability, high CK → NMS; stop drug, supportive ICU care
Severe NMS: dantrolene/bromocriptine; olanzapine/clozapine: weight gain, diabetes, dyslipidemia
Risperidone: ↑prolactin; ziprasidone: ↑QT; clozapine: neutropenia, myocarditis, ileus, seizures

rows.label: Avoid
items: Lewy body/Parkinson disease: severe sensitivity; specialist-selected quetiapine/clozapine if essential
Dementia: ↑mortality, falls; dangerous behavior after safer measures → low-dose **quetiapine**/risperidone, not benzodiazepines

rows.label: Interactions
items: Other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte depletion → torsades; sedatives/alcohol increase CNS depression
Metoclopramide, prochlorperazine block dopamine: same EPS, tardive dyskinesia, NMS; avoid after NMS

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Weight/BMI, BP, glucose/A1c, lipids; movement examinations; **ANC with clozapine**
ECG for cardiac/QT risks; prolactin when symptomatic; ask about bowel function
Clozapine + ANC <1000 → **hold clozapine**, not dose reduction; ANC 1000–1499 → continue, closer monitoring

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Anticholinergics worsen tardive dyskinesia**; valbenazine/deutetrabenazine are VMAT2 inhibitors
Akathisia can mimic worsening agitation; increasing antipsychotic dose can worsen it
Low-potency FGAs: more orthostasis/anticholinergic effects; high-potency FGAs: more EPS

table.title: Extrapyramidal syndromes
rows: Stop/switch culprit first; benztropine or amantadine

antipsychotics.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [FDA clozapine monitoring update](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-removes-risk-evaluation-and-mitigation-strategy-rems-program-antipsychotic-drug-clozapine); other effects established teaching.

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.scope: Acute appendicitis, clinical presentation, pediatric and pregnancy considerations, imaging (ultrasound, CT), surgical management
appendicitis.core: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, followed by anorexia and nausea, suggests appendiceal inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescents/young adults; luminal obstruction by lymphoid hyperplasia or fecalith
Older adults may have obstructing neoplasm; immunosuppression can blunt findings

rows.label: Clues
items: McBurney tenderness, guarding, fever; Rovsing, psoas, or obturator signs depend on position
★ **Diffuse peritonitis, toxicity, hypotension** → perforation/sepsis until proven otherwise
Young children: nonspecific symptoms and rapid progression; pregnancy: displaced appendix, less reliable examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal obstruction → distention, venous congestion, bacterial invasion → ischemia/perforation
Visceral midgut pain precedes focal parietal peritoneal irritation

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, urinalysis, **pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; pyuria does not exclude appendicitis
★ Stable nonpregnant adult → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** when diagnosis uncertain
★ Child/pregnancy → **ultrasound first**; nondiagnostic → MRI without gadolinium, or CT in nonpregnant child
Noncompressible enlarged appendix >6 mm with periappendiceal inflammation supports diagnosis
Clear peritonitis → surgical evaluation; do not delay necessary operation for repeated imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ NPO, **IV fluids, IV opioids, ceftriaxone + metronidazole**, surgical consultation; opioids do not obscure exam
Laparoscopic appendectomy definitive; do not withhold necessary surgery during pregnancy
Selected uncomplicated cases → antibiotics after shared decision; recurrence/failure higher, especially with appendicolith
Localized abscess/phlegmon in stable patient → antibiotics ± image-guided drainage; follow-up based on age/risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Perforation, abscess, peritonitis, sepsis, ileus
Postoperative wound infection, intra-abdominal collection, adhesional obstruction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, adnexal findings
Ovarian torsion: sudden unilateral pelvic pain; gastroenteritis: diarrhea prominent before diffuse cramping
Mesenteric adenitis: viral prodrome, normal appendix on imaging

appendicitis.evidence: Not checked online; established general-surgery evaluation and treatment principles.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: **Family history of asthma/atopy**: strongest childhood risk; allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking
Cough-variant: isolated chronic cough, worse with cold/exercise; normal examination and radiograph

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links IgE on **mast cells** → histamine, leukotrienes → bronchoconstriction
Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis
PFT pattern: ↓FEV1, normal/↓FVC, normal/↑TLC from air trapping

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral
Discharge: **PEF ≥70–80% predicted** (less wheeze is unreliable) + 5–7 day **oral prednisone** prevents relapse

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ GINA: **no SABA-only treatment**, no LABA monotherapy; ICS with every reliever use
Older exam questions (NAEPP) may expect: symptoms ≤2 days/week, awakenings ≤2/month → **SABA alone**; more → daily ICS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings
Deconditioning: obese/sedentary, exertional dyspnea; normal PFTs, no bronchodilator response

atrial-fibrillation.name: Atrial fibrillation
atrial-fibrillation.scope: Rate and rhythm control, stroke prevention (CHA2DS2-VASc), unstable AF, embolic complications
atrial-fibrillation.core: Disorganized atrial activation produces an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm and left atrial appendage thromboembolism risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, hypertension, heart failure, coronary disease, obesity, sleep apnea
Hyperthyroidism, alcohol binges, infection, postoperative stress, mitral valve disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Palpitations, exercise intolerance, dyspnea; sometimes incidental or first detected after stroke
★ **Hypotension, ischemic chest pain, pulmonary edema, altered mentation** → unstable AF
Very rapid irregular wide-complex rhythm suggests preexcitation; ordinary AV nodal blockers can be dangerous

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pulmonary-vein ectopic triggers plus atrial remodeling sustain reentry
Loss of atrial contraction reduces filling; persistent tachycardia can impair LV function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG: absent discrete P waves**, variable RR intervals; document rhythm rather than pulse alone
TSH, electrolytes, renal function; transthoracic echocardiogram for ventricular function and structural disease
Intermittent symptoms → ambulatory rhythm monitoring; assess reversible triggers

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → **synchronized cardioversion**; do not delay for anticoagulation or TEE
Stable rate control: metoprolol or diltiazem; avoid diltiazem/verapamil with reduced EF
Decompensated HF: digoxin or amiodarone; preexcited AF: procainamide or cardioversion, no AV nodal blockers
Rhythm control for symptoms, early disease, or HF: cardioversion, selected antiarrhythmics, catheter ablation
★ Duration ≥48 hours/unknown: **3 weeks anticoagulation or TEE** before elective cardioversion; ≥4 weeks afterward

rows.label: Complications
items: **Top risk factor for cardioembolic stroke**, above age/hypertension; limb/gut emboli; tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy
Anticoagulant bleeding; rhythm drugs may cause proarrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Long-term anticoagulation: **CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥2 men/≥3 women**; consider one point lower
Apixaban/other DOAC preferred; mechanical valve or moderate/severe rheumatic mitral stenosis → warfarin
Weight reduction, BP/OSA treatment, limit alcohol
Aspirin no substitute for anticoagulation; adding aspirin to warfarin/DOAC → **more bleeding**, no added stroke protection

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atrial flutter: sawtooth atrial activity, often regular 2:1 conduction
Multifocal atrial tachycardia: ≥3 P-wave morphologies, isoelectric intervals

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess
**Cracked, excoriated nipples** → main portal of entry for lactational mastitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: cystic lactational/postlactational mass, no inflammation, varies with feeds; fat–fluid level on imaging
Mastitis: focal tender erythema, fever, no fluctuance; abscess adds **fluctuance**; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → usually **papilloma**; exclude malignancy, persistent → surgical evaluation
Nonbloody discharge only on expression, normal exam → **physiologic**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma
Cyclic bilateral nodularity, no dominant mass → **reexamine after menses**, before imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Painful simple cyst → aspiration; nonbloody fluid + full collapse → benign; bloody fluid/residual mass → **biopsy**
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Breast pain, no mass, young, normal exam → **reassurance**; fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID
★ Mastitis → **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**, keep breastfeeding/pumping; abscess → add needle/incision drainage; MRSA → clindamycin
Tender lactating lump, no erythema/fever → **warm compresses**, keep nursing; persistent galactocele → aspiration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

table.title: Common benign findings
rows: Early postpartum; bilateral tense tender breasts, low fever

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.scope: Lower urinary tract symptoms, medical therapy, urinary retention and obstructive uropathy
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.core: Aging man with hesitancy, weak stream, incomplete emptying, and nocturia from benign periurethral prostatic enlargement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, androgen exposure, family history, obesity/metabolic syndrome
Anticholinergics, opioids, and sympathomimetic decongestants can precipitate retention

rows.label: Clues
items: Storage symptoms: urgency, frequency; voiding symptoms: straining, intermittency, terminal dribbling
Smooth, symmetric enlarged prostate; size correlates imperfectly with symptom severity
★ **Painful inability to void** with palpable bladder → acute urinary retention
Renal dysfunction or bilateral hydronephrosis suggests high-pressure obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dihydrotestosterone-driven transition-zone hyperplasia + alpha-adrenergic smooth-muscle tone obstruct bladder outlet

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**, symptom score, examination; review medications and neurologic disease
Postvoid residual if incomplete emptying suspected; creatinine/renal ultrasound for obstruction or renal impairment
PSA after shared decision-making if result changes management; elevation not specific for cancer

rows.label: Tx
items: Mild, nonbothersome → observation; reduce evening fluids, caffeine, alcohol; timed voiding
★ Acute retention → **urethral catheter**, then alpha-blocker and voiding trial; suprapubic drainage if catheterization fails
★ Refractory symptoms, retention, recurrent UTIs, stones, renal impairment → **TURP or other outlet procedure**
Monitor urine output/electrolytes after relief of prolonged obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Overflow incontinence, recurrent infection, bladder stones, postrenal AKI
Postobstructive diuresis; surgery → bleeding, retrograde ejaculation, urethral stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid precipitating drugs; reassess progressive symptoms and residual volume
BPH does not transform into prostate cancer; continue independent cancer-risk discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Prostate cancer: hard asymmetric nodule
Prostatitis: tender prostate, fever; neurogenic bladder: neurologic disease, altered bladder sensation

table.title: Medication selection
rows: Large gland; reduce progression over months

bipolar-disorder.name: Bipolar disorder
bipolar-disorder.scope: Bipolar I (manic episode, DIG FAST), bipolar II (hypomania and major depression), cyclothymic disorder, acute mania pharmacotherapy (antipsychotics, lithium, valproate), maintenance therapy
bipolar-disorder.core: Distinct episodes of pathologically increased energy with elevated or irritable mood distinguish bipolar illness from ordinary mood variability.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong family history; typical onset adolescence/young adulthood
Sleep deprivation, antidepressants, stimulants, substances can precipitate episodes

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **DIG FAST**: distractibility, impulsivity, grandiosity, flight of ideas, activity, decreased sleep need, talkativeness
≥3 associated symptoms; ≥4 if mood only irritable
Mania: psychosis, marked impairment, risky spending/sex, or hospitalization; reduced sleep without fatigue

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial genetic vulnerability with dysregulated mood, reward and circadian systems

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical longitudinal history + collateral**; ask about prior elevated episodes before treating depression
Assess suicidality, pregnancy, substance use; TSH, metabolic panel, toxicology to exclude secondary causes
Hospitalization requirement can establish manic duration criterion even before one week
Major depression ≥2 weeks; hypomania causes no psychosis, marked impairment or hospitalization
Cyclothymia: symptoms ≥half the time; no symptom-free interval >2 months or full mood episodes

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute mania → **antipsychotic** (olanzapine/quetiapine); severe → add lithium/valproate; mixed/rapid cycling → **divalproex**
Unsafe, psychotic, severely agitated, or unable to care for self → hospitalization
Depression → quetiapine, lurasidone, lithium, lamotrigine; urgent/refractory or first-trimester psychotic mania → **ECT**
★ **Avoid antidepressant monotherapy**; lamotrigine does not treat acute mania
Maintenance: lithium, quetiapine, valproate or lamotrigine selected by episode pattern; lithium reduces suicide risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, substance misuse, financial/relationship loss; metabolic adverse effects of antipsychotics
Lithium: renal/thyroid toxicity; valproate/carbamazepine: teratogenicity, avoid in first trimester; lamotrigine: severe rash

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular sleep, psychoeducation, relapse-sign monitoring, maintenance adherence; avoid stimulants and substance misuse

rows.label: Mimics
items: ADHD: chronic baseline symptoms rather than distinct mood episodes
Borderline personality: brief reactive shifts linked to interpersonal stress
Medication/substance-induced mania: onset after antidepressant, stimulant, steroid → **stop culprit first**
Hyperthyroidism: heat intolerance, tremor, low TSH

table.title: Diagnostic branches
rows: Hypomania ≥4 days + major depression; never mania

bone-tumors.name: Bone tumors
bone-tumors.scope: Osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, chondrosarcoma, giant cell tumor of bone, osteochondroma, osteoid osteoma, bone metastases, biopsy
bone-tumors.core: Persistent focal bone pain, a growing mass, or a destructive radiographic lesion requires planned evaluation before biopsy or fixation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Osteosarcoma: adolescence, hereditary retinoblastoma (RB1), prior radiation, Paget disease; chondrosarcoma: older adults
Hereditary multiple exostoses predispose to osteochondromas; most adult malignant bone lesions are metastases

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Night/rest pain**, enlarging mass, constitutional symptoms or pathologic fracture → concerning lesion
Osteoid osteoma: nocturnal pain relieved by NSAIDs; small cortical nidus
Osteochondroma: painless metaphyseal exostosis with medullary continuity; new growth after maturity concerning
Known cancer + constant back pain, vertebral point tenderness → **spinal metastasis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tumor lineage determines osteoid, cartilage or primitive-cell production; aggressive growth destroys cortex
Giant cell tumor: neoplastic stromal cells recruit osteoclast-like giant cells, causing locally aggressive osteolysis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Plain radiographs first**; assess location, margins, periosteal reaction and matrix
Aggressive lesion → MRI entire involved bone/adjacent joint; chest CT for lung metastases
★ **Orthopedic oncology plans biopsy tract**; core biopsy after imaging, before definitive treatment
CBC, ESR/CRP if infection suspected; normal labs do not exclude malignancy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Osteosarcoma → **neoadjuvant chemotherapy + wide resection**, then postoperative chemotherapy
Ewing → systemic chemotherapy plus surgery and/or radiation
Chondrosarcoma → wide surgical excision; conventional tumors relatively chemo/radioresistant
Symptomatic osteoid osteoma → radiofrequency ablation; asymptomatic osteochondroma → observation
Giant cell tumor → curettage/reconstruction; selected unresectable lesions → denosumab

rows.label: Complications
items: Pathologic fracture, neurovascular compromise, pulmonary metastases; limb surgery and chemotherapy morbidity
Mandible metastasis → mental nerve anesthesia (**numb chin**)

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: infection markers, cultures; may closely resemble Ewing
Bone metastases: older adult, multiple lesions; myeloma: anemia, monoclonal protein
Unicameral bone cyst: child, lucent expansile proximal humerus lesion; pathologic fracture after minor trauma

bone-tumors.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

bowel-obstruction.name: Bowel obstruction
bowel-obstruction.scope: Small bowel obstruction (adhesions, hernia), large bowel obstruction (volvulus, malignancy), paralytic ileus, NG decompression, surgical management
bowel-obstruction.core: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, distention, and obstipation suggest mechanical obstruction; constant pain or systemic toxicity raises concern for strangulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior abdominal surgery (**adhesions**, leading cause), incarcerated hernia, Crohn strictures → small-bowel obstruction
Colorectal malignancy, chronic constipation, institutionalization → large-bowel obstruction or sigmoid volvulus
Recent surgery, opioids, hypokalemia, severe systemic illness → ileus

rows.label: Clues
items: Early high-pitched sounds may become absent; proximal obstruction causes earlier vomiting, distal disease greater distention
★ **Peritonitis, fever, tachycardia, rising lactate**, or continuous severe pain → ischemia/perforation
Complete → **obstipation**, no flatus; partial may still pass stool/diarrhea, not excluding obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal blockage → upstream dilation, third spacing; closed loop compromises venous then arterial supply
Adynamic ileus reflects impaired motility without an anatomic transition point

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** defines transition point, cause, and ischemic signs
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, lactate; normal lactate cannot exclude early ischemia
Radiograph may show dilated loops/air-fluid levels, no rectal gas; CT more definitive if diagnosis uncertain
★ Massive colonic distention + **coffee-bean (inverted-U) loop** on radiograph → sigmoid volvulus
Pregnancy: plain radiograph acceptable first (minimal fetal dose); MRI if unclear; do not delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO, IV isotonic fluids, electrolyte correction**; NG decompression for significant vomiting/distention
★ Strangulation, perforation, closed loop, or incarcerated hernia → **urgent surgery** + ceftriaxone/metronidazole
Uncomplicated adhesive SBO → surgical observation, serial examination; water-soluble contrast helps predict resolution
Failure to improve during a short monitored trial, commonly up to 72 h → operation
Ileus → correct trigger, reduce opioids, mobilize; no operation solely for absent sounds

rows.label: Complications
items: Dehydration, AKI, hypokalemic alkalosis; bowel necrosis, perforation, sepsis
Recurrent adhesions; short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early postoperative ambulation, opioid-sparing analgesia, electrolyte correction; elective repair of symptomatic hernias

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gastroenteritis: prominent diarrhea, no focal transition point
Mesenteric ischemia: pain out of proportion before peritoneal signs
Ileus: hypoactive/absent sounds, gas throughout bowel including rectum
Diabetic autonomic neuropathy: dysmotility, dilated loops without transition point

table.title: Large-bowel branches
rows: Sigmoidoscopic detorsion, rectal tube → same-admission resection

bowel-obstruction.evidence: Not checked online; established acute surgical management principles.

brain-tumors.name: Brain tumors
brain-tumors.scope: Metastatic brain tumors, glioblastoma, meningioma, pediatric tumors (medulloblastoma), vestibular schwannoma
brain-tumors.core: Progressive focal deficits, new seizures or headache with raised intracranial pressure require brain imaging for a mass lesion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Known lung, breast, melanoma, renal or colorectal malignancy → brain metastases
Prior cranial radiation; NF 2 predisposes to bilateral vestibular schwannomas and meningiomas

rows.label: Clues
items: Morning headache, vomiting, papilledema; altered consciousness or pupillary asymmetry → impending herniation
Frontal → personality change; posterior fossa → ataxia; temporal (Meyer loop) → contralateral **superior quadrantanopia**
Pediatric posterior fossa mass can obstruct CSF flow and rapidly cause hydrocephalus
★ **Anosmia**, normal nasal exam, frontal release signs, papilledema → **subfrontal olfactory groove meningioma**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tumor disrupts local brain function and blood–brain barrier → vasogenic edema
Fixed cranial volume makes expanding tissue/CSF raise pressure and threaten brainstem perfusion
Astrocytoma grade, prognosis → **degree of histologic anaplasia**, not metastasis; extracranial spread rare

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Contrast MRI brain** best defines mass, edema and multiplicity; CT for unstable patients
Metastatic pattern → search primary with chest/abdominal imaging; tissue diagnosis when needed
★ Suspected mass with pressure signs → **avoid LP** until safe after imaging
Tinnitus, imbalance, facial weakness/numbness, altered taste (CN VII, V) → audiometry and MRI internal auditory canals

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic edema → **dexamethasone**; herniation → head elevation, hypertonic saline/mannitol, emergency neurosurgery
Seizure → levetiracetam; no routine antiseizure prophylaxis for every seizure-naive tumor patient
★ **Resection versus radiation** depends on lesion, symptoms, accessibility and systemic disease
Medulloblastoma → resection, chemotherapy and usually craniospinal radiation; avoid/delay radiation in very young children
Craniopharyngioma resection disrupts pituitary stalk → **lifelong pituitary hormone replacement**; watch central DI

rows.label: Complications
items: Obstructive hydrocephalus, herniation, hemorrhage, persistent neurologic deficits
Radiation injury, cognitive decline, steroid hyperglycemia and infection

rows.label: Mimics
items: Abscess: infection context and central diffusion restriction
Primary CNS lymphoma: often periventricular; steroids can obscure biopsy
Stroke: abrupt maximal onset with vascular distribution; chronic subdural: prior head trauma
Ménière disease: episodic vertigo, fluctuating low-frequency hearing loss

table.title: Tumor distinctions
rows: Months of headache, deficits; necrotic, crosses corpus callosum
Woman; extra-axial, uniform enhancement, dural tail; parasagittal
Child; midline cerebellar mass; CSF drop metastases
CPA; insidious, high-frequency unilateral sensorineural hearing loss
Child; ataxia, nystagmus, head tilt, cranial neuropathies

brain-tumors.evidence: Not checked online; established neuro-oncology teaching.

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, close-relative family history (distant relative adds little), prior chest irradiation
**Combined estrogen-progestin therapy**, prolonged estrogen, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; **full-thickness biopsy**, investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core biopsy of suspicious lesion; pregnancy → **ultrasound first**
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease, including microinvasion ≤1 mm → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer
Axillary node adenocarcinoma, normal mammogram → occult breast primary; breast MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; **positive margins → reexcision** before adjuvant therapy
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment, monitor LVEF; triple-negative → chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab if higher-risk
Locally advanced → neoadjuvant treatment, then surgery/radiation; large residual + palpable nodes → **mastectomy + axillary dissection**
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone (often **mixed lytic–blastic**), lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy
Prior cancer + severe hypercalcemia, lytic lesions → recurrence; thiazide/calcium supplements cause only mild elevation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells
Surveillance/risk reduction if concordant; later cancer usually ductal

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

bronchiectasis.name: Bronchiectasis
bronchiectasis.scope: Cystic fibrosis, post-infectious, high-resolution CT, airway clearance, pseudomonas colonization, acute exacerbation
bronchiectasis.core: Chronic productive cough with recurrent respiratory infections and permanently dilated bronchi on high-resolution CT.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cystic fibrosis, prior severe pneumonia/TB, primary ciliary dyskinesia, aspiration, immunodeficiency
ABPA, rheumatoid arthritis, obstructing endobronchial lesion; some cases remain idiopathic

rows.label: Clues
items: Copious purulent sputum, coarse crackles, recurrent focal infections, hemoptysis, sometimes clubbing
Exacerbation: increased sputum volume/purulence, cough, dyspnea, fatigue; hypoxemia or sepsis → severe disease
Early lifelong infections, sinusitis, infertility, or situs inversus suggest impaired ciliary clearance
Child: chronic cough refractory to bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics + persistent focal collapse/consolidation → localized bronchiectasis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired mucus clearance → persistent infection and neutrophilic inflammation → irreversible airway wall destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **High-resolution chest CT**: signet-ring bronchi, absent tapering, airways visible near pleura, cystic spaces ± air-fluid levels
Sputum bacterial and mycobacterial cultures; spirometry measures associated airflow limitation
Quantitative immunoglobulins; total IgE/Aspergillus testing for ABPA; sweat chloride if CF suspected
Localized disease → bronchoscopy for tumor/foreign body; diffuse disease → investigate systemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, exercise; bronchodilator for obstruction; no routine inhaled steroids or non-CF dornase alfa
★ Exacerbation → sputum culture then antibiotics guided by prior isolates; often **14 days**
Pseudomonas susceptible → ciprofloxacin; severe infection → IV cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam
★ ≥2 yearly or ≥1 severe exacerbation → azithromycin after NTM exclusion; chronic Pseudomonas → inhaled tobramycin
Massive hemoptysis → airway protection and bronchial artery embolization; focal refractory disease → resection evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic Pseudomonas colonization, resistant infection, respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension
Antibiotic toxicity/resistance; macrolides can cause QT prolongation and hearing impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, aspiration management, treatment of underlying immunodeficiency
New Pseudomonas isolation → specialist eradication regimen, often ciprofloxacin followed by inhaled antibiotic

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chronic bronchitis: smoking-related sputum without characteristic bronchial dilation
Lung abscess: solitary cavity with air-fluid level; no lifelong productive cough
Pulmonary TB: constitutional illness and compatible imaging; mycobacterial testing confirms

candidiasis.name: Candidiasis
candidiasis.scope: Oropharyngeal candidiasis (thrush), diaper candidiasis, intertrigo, vulvovaginal candidiasis, cell-mediated vs neutrophil immunity, nystatin, fluconazole
candidiasis.core: Opportunistic yeast overgrowth on mucosa or moist skin; distribution and host immune defects determine evaluation and antifungal route.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent antibiotics, diabetes, pregnancy, inhaled/systemic steroids, HIV; infants, dentures, skin occlusion
Neutropenia, central venous catheters, parenteral nutrition → invasive infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Odynophagia or dysphagia with immunosuppression** → esophageal involvement, even without visible oral lesions
Persistent/recurrent thrush outside infancy → evaluate HIV, diabetes, or other immune defects
Sepsis in neutropenic or catheterized host → consider candidemia rather than isolated superficial disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **T-cell/IL-17 dysfunction → mucocutaneous disease; neutrophil defects → invasive candidiasis**
Candida albicans: budding yeast and pseudohyphae; overgrowth of endogenous flora rather than routine sexual transmission

rows.label: Dx
items: Typical oral/cutaneous disease → clinical diagnosis; uncertain lesions → KOH microscopy
★ Vaginal symptoms → wet mount/KOH; **pH usually <4.5**; negative microscopy with suspicion → culture
Complicated/recurrent vaginitis → culture/speciation; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: Esophageal disease → **systemic fluconazole 14–21 days**; refractory symptoms → endoscopy with biopsy
★ Pregnancy → **7-day intravaginal clotrimazole**; systemic triazoles contraindicated
Recurrent vaginitis ≥3 episodes/year → extended induction then weekly fluconazole for 6 months
Candidemia → IV micafungin and blood cultures; investigate/remove infected catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Poor oral intake, painful fissures, recurrent vaginitis; invasive disease → endophthalmitis, endocarditis, organ abscesses
Azoles: hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation, CYP interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rinse mouth after inhaled steroids; clean dentures, keep folds dry, change wet diapers promptly
Optimize glucose control and HIV ART; routine partner treatment unnecessary for uncomplicated vaginitis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Leukoplakia/oral hairy leukoplakia: white plaques do not scrape off
Irritant diaper dermatitis: spares folds; bacterial vaginosis: fishy odor, elevated vaginal pH

table.title: Superficial presentations
rows: Beefy erythema, satellite pustules; folds involved
Topical azole or single-dose oral fluconazole

cardiomyopathies.name: Cardiomyopathies
cardiomyopathies.scope: Dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, restrictive cardiomyopathy, stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, viral myocarditis, diagnostic evaluation, management
cardiomyopathies.core: Myocardial disease causes pump failure, impaired filling, dynamic obstruction, or arrhythmias; echocardiography defines the phenotype.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dilated: familial disease, alcohol, anthracyclines, peripartum state, **viral myocarditis**
Hypertrophic: autosomal dominant sarcomeric variants; restrictive: amyloid, hemochromatosis, radiation
Takotsubo: emotional/physical stress; myocarditis: recent viral illness, immune checkpoint inhibitors

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, edema, elevated JVP; **displaced PMI**, S3 → dilated LV; syncope/ventricular arrhythmia signals danger
★ Obstructive HCM murmur **↑Valsalva/standing**, ↓squatting/handgrip; exertional presyncope
Myocarditis: chest discomfort, tachycardia disproportionate to fever, acute heart failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sarcomere dysfunction or myocardial injury → remodeling; infiltration → reduced ventricular compliance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG, troponin, BNP → transthoracic echo**; assess coronary ischemia when suspected
Cardiac MRI: inflammation, scar, infiltrative patterns; iron studies or monoclonal protein testing when relevant
Endomyocardial biopsy: selected fulminant unexplained failure, malignant arrhythmias, suspected giant-cell myocarditis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ HFrEF: **ARNI, evidence-based beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor**; loop diuretic for congestion
Obstructive HCM: nonvasodilating beta-blocker (propranolol, metoprolol); alternative verapamil/diltiazem
Refractory obstruction → myosin inhibitor, disopyramide, or septal reduction; avoid dehydration and vasodilators
Restrictive disease: cautious diuresis, treat cause; Takotsubo: supportive care after excluding ACS
Myocarditis with shock → ICU, circulatory support; no routine antiviral or immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Sudden cardiac death, atrial fibrillation, thromboembolism; advanced failure → transplantation evaluation
★ HCM with cardiac arrest or major sudden-death risk → **ICD** consideration

rows.label: Prevention
items: Screen first-degree relatives in inherited disease; avoid cardiotoxins
Myocarditis: restrict strenuous exercise until clinical recovery and reassessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic cardiomyopathy: obstructive coronary disease explains dysfunction
Constrictive pericarditis: pericardial disease, respiratory ventricular interdependence
Aortic stenosis: murmur softer with standing/Valsalva, unlike obstructive HCM

table.title: Echo phenotype
rows: Enlarged ventricles, diffuse hypokinesia, reduced EF
Transient apical ballooning beyond coronary territory

cardiomyopathies.evidence: HCM checked 2026-10-30: [AHA/ACC 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/05/06/15/12/2024-hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy-gl); other content established teaching.

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.name: Catheter-related bloodstream infection
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.scope: Central line infection, organisms, line removal, prevention
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.core: Fever or rigors in a patient with an intravascular catheter, especially during infusion, raises concern for catheter-related bacteremia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long catheter dwell time, femoral placement, parenteral nutrition, immunosuppression, hemodialysis
Poor asepsis, frequent hub manipulation; tunneled devices and ports also susceptible

rows.label: Clues
items: Exit-site erythema or drainage may occur; normal insertion-site appearance does not exclude infection
★ **Hypotension, persistent bacteremia**, new murmur, or embolic signs → complicated infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Skin flora migrate externally or contaminated hubs seed intraluminal biofilm
Biofilm limits antibiotic penetration; S aureus and Candida frequently seed distant sites

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Before antibiotics: **paired peripheral and catheter blood cultures**, labelled by source
Same organism with catheter culture positive ≥2 h earlier supports catheter source
Culture removed catheter tip when infection suspected; no routine tip culture after elective removal
Repeat blood cultures to document clearance; persistent positivity → endocarditis, infected thrombus, abscess evaluation
S aureus bacteremia → echocardiography, TEE when high risk; assess metastatic foci

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric **IV vancomycin** (MRSA, coagulase-negative staph); sepsis/neutropenia → add cefepime; adjust to cultures
★ **Remove line** for shock, tunnel infection, endocarditis, persistent bacteremia, S aureus, Pseudomonas, or fungi
Candida → echinocandin; MSSA → cefazolin or nafcillin; enterococcal treatment follows susceptibilities
Selected stable long-term line infections with coagulase-negative staphylococci → systemic antibiotics + antibiotic lock
Uncomplicated S aureus bacteremia: ≥14 days after clearance; endocarditis/deep infection usually requires 4–6 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Endocarditis, septic thrombophlebitis, osteomyelitis, septic emboli, shock
Unnecessary device retention → relapse; repeated placement → thrombosis and vascular injury
Suppurative thrombophlebitis: fluctuant, purulent vein after line removal → **surgical vein excision**, not compresses

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hand hygiene, chlorhexidine skin preparation, maximal sterile barrier** during insertion
Scrub hubs, sterile dressings, daily necessity review, prompt removal of unnecessary lines
Avoid routine prophylactic systemic antibiotics or scheduled catheter replacement solely to prevent infection

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contaminated blood culture: single skin-flora isolate without corroborating cultures or illness
Infusate reaction: temporal symptoms without reproducible bacteremia
Catheter thrombosis: swelling, poor flow; cultures negative unless infected
Wound/abdominal source: local findings; benign exam + gram-positive bacteremia → catheter

table.title: Organism pattern
rows: S epidermidis: leading biofilm/port-pocket infection; distinguish contamination
Parenteral nutrition, broad antibiotics; remove catheter

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.evidence: Not checked online; established catheter-infection management principles.

cervical-cancer-screening.name: Cervical Cancer Screening
cervical-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF guidelines by age (Pap smear alone 21-29, Pap with hrHPV cotesting or hrHPV alone 30-65), screening cessation, post-hysterectomy
cervical-cancer-screening.core: Screen average-risk people with a cervix from age 21; age, prior results, and cervical precancer history determine testing and cessation.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **Average-risk cervix present**; sexual history and HPV vaccination do not alter schedule
